newsitem.title: USA: Minn. stadium initiative falls short of ballot.
newsitem.headline: Minn. stadium initiative falls short of ballot.

text.p: A Minnesota political group's initiative requiring voter approval for major Minneapolis funding of professional sports facilities has fallen short of ballot requirements, a city election official said Friday.
Progressive Minnesota had 5,090 valid signatures on its city-wide petition and under state law has another 10 days to meet ballot requirements, elections Director Joyce Swadner said.
The group needs 8,155 registered voters to place the charter amendment on the November ballot, Swadner said. If the group fails to gather those signatures by Aug. 25, the initiative dies, she said.
The ballot initiative would require a popular vote if public contributions to professional sports facilities total $10 million or more.

The proposed amendment would not impede construction of a proposed $400 million Minnesota Twins stadium if financing is approved before the general election, but would set an important precedent even if it does not influence the ballpark debate, a Progressive Minnesota spokeswoman said.
